init.title: Australia and New Zealand Disaster Watch options

menu_options.forecasts: Forecast signals and AI rain outlook
menu_options.add_river_point: Add a river flood forecast point

settings.title: Monitoring settings
settings.description: Adjust spatial perimeter radius, emergency warning overrides, and council dashboard endpoints.

forecasts.title: Forecast signals (model-derived, not official)
forecasts.description: Optional signals calculated from Open-Meteo model forecasts for your location. They are not official warnings and do not replace BoM, MetService or emergency service warnings or the official fire danger rating. Open-Meteo's free API is for non-commercial use only (CC BY 4.0).

data.ai_ensemble: Experimental AI ensemble rain outlook (ECMWF AIFS)

data_description.weather_signals: Hourly forecast of maximum wind gust, maximum apparent temperature, thunderstorm potential and a calculated (not official) fire danger index for the next 24 hours.
data_description.gust_threshold: The damaging gusts forecast turns on when the forecast gust reaches this speed. BoM's damaging wind criterion is 90 km/h.
data_description.heat_threshold: The extreme heat forecast turns on when the forecast apparent temperature reaches this value.
data_description.ai_ensemble: Experimental AI model output, fetched every 6 hours. Shows the share of ensemble members forecasting heavy rain.
data_description.ai_weathernext: Experimental. Adds Google WeatherNext 2 (every 12 hours). Whether Google's experimental data terms apply to data served by Open-Meteo is unverified. Ignored unless the AI rain outlook is on.
data_description.heavy_rain_threshold: A member counts as heavy rain when its 24-hour total reaches this amount.

add_river_point.title: Add a river flood forecast point
add_river_point.description: Pick a point on a river. GloFAS models rivers on a 5 km grid, so a point next to a small creek or in a city centre may have no data; a nearby river cell is then suggested. Flood data by Open-Meteo.com (GloFAS), non-commercial use only.

river_suggestion.title: Use a nearby river cell?
river_suggestion.description: The selected point is not on the GloFAS river grid. The nearby cell with the largest discharge is {distance} km away at {latitude}, {longitude} (mean forecast discharge {discharge} m³/s).

river_threshold.title: Flood risk threshold for {name}
river_threshold.description: The flood risk sensor turns on when any ensemble member forecasts discharge above this threshold within the horizon. The default is this cell's median annual peak discharge over the last 20 years of the GloFAS reanalysis (about a 2-year flood): {baseline}.

edit_river_point_details.title: Edit {name}
edit_river_point_details.description: Median annual peak discharge (about a 2-year flood): {baseline}. To move a point, remove it and add a new one.

earthquakes.title: Earthquakes
earthquakes.description: Optional earthquake hazards from Geoscience Australia (CC BY 4.0). Quakes of magnitude 3 or more from the last 48 hours within the monitoring radius are shown: M6 or more as Watch and Act, M4.5 or more as Advice, smaller ones as Information.

river_gauges.title: River and creek level gauges
river_gauges.description: Choose gauges to add as water level sensors. The list shows the nearest gauges within the monitoring radius that reported a level in the last 6 hours, with their distance and current level. Leave all unticked for no gauge sensors. Gauges are polled every 15 minutes. Searching can take up to a minute the first time.

data_description.river_gauges: Levels are in metres above each gauge's local datum, not above sea level. Sources: Queensland Water Monitoring Information Portal, WaterNSW and New Zealand regional council Hilltop servers.

river_alert_levels.title: Gauge alert levels
river_alert_levels.description: Optionally enter an alert level in metres for each gauge, on the same datum as its water level sensor (for example the minor flood level from your council or the Bureau of Meteorology). A gauge with a level gets a binary sensor that turns on while the water is at or above it. Leave a field blank for no alert sensor.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Open-Meteo. Try again later.
error.duplicate_river_point: Enter a name that no other river point uses.
error.empty_river_point_name: Enter a name for the river point.
error.no_river_cell: No river cell with data was found near this point. Pick a point on or next to a larger river.
error.invalid_threshold: The threshold must be greater than 0.
error.rivers_unavailable: The gauge services could not be reached, so only the gauges you already selected are listed. Try again later.
error.no_river_gauges: No gauge within the monitoring radius reported a level in the last 6 hours. Increase the radius to search further.

abort.too_many_river_points: You can add up to 10 river points. Remove one first.
abort.river_point_not_found: This river point no longer exists.

feeds_unavailable.message: All emergency hazard feeds are unavailable: {feeds}

river_gauges_unavailable.message: None of the selected river gauges could be reached

card_resource_cleanup_failed.title: Dashboard card resource could not be removed
card_resource_cleanup_failed.description: The last Australia and New Zealand Disaster Watch entry was deleted, but Home Assistant could not remove the dashboard card resource `{url}`. It is retried a few times while Home Assistant runs. If this issue remains, remove the resource under **Settings > Dashboards > Resources**, then ignore this issue. Adding the integration again also fixes it.
